description: OpenTideConstants SDK API manifest (SDK spec section 4). Every public operation, attribute, argument, default, enum value and error code, by its snake_case name. Each SDK's CI turns the names into its own form by the naming rules below and compares them with its public surface; a missing or an extra name fails CI. Names in pending_port are not built yet in that language and must be absent.

naming.ruby: methods and options snake_case; a predicate is_x is x?; an operation with mutating true ends in !; aliases.ruby are extra idiom names for the same operation
naming.python: snake_case; a predicate is_x is a property; options are keyword-only
naming.typescript: methods, predicates and options in camelCase: split the snake_case name on _, capitalise the first letter of each part after the first, join (station_by_alias -> stationByAlias, radius_km -> radiusKm, is_reference -> isReference getter); kind field members (data fields) keep snake_case; operations with typescript_async true return a Promise
naming.c: otc_ + snake_case; an operation's c gives its C function name(s) where the spec names them (a slash separates several functions); a c of the form f(p) names the parameter p of the function f (UpdateResult: the out-parameters of otc_fetch_update); a field of an object with c type T is the accessor T_<field> (otc_station_lat), or a struct member when c_struct is true; enum values are OTC_<ENUM>_<VALUE> plus OTC_<ENUM>_OTHER; error codes map to otc_status values in errors[].c

kinds.attribute: a value with no args (Ruby method, Python property, TypeScript getter or property)
kinds.field: a data field with the schema's snake_case name in every language

after_close: After close, every call on the client or its Release (every query and every release-management operation; close itself excepted) raises io (FileError, message "the release is closed"), the same in eager and stream mode, and no automatic update runs (spec 4.2, 5.6, CR D21). Scope (CR2 DR32): the in-memory metadata getters (datestamp, created, format_version, citation, files, and the client's release property) stay readable after close; every station query, every iterator step, stats, attribution, reference_station and subordinates_of fail with io, and an iterator checks on each step. This rule applies to every operation in this manifest, so it is stated once here and not added to each errors list.

args.note: open a local .json, .json.gz or .jsonl (+ .meta.json); TypeScript: Node only. The name must be OTC_<D><ext> (D a valid datestamp, ext one of these), otherwise invalid_argument; file together with release, offline or on_network_error is invalid_argument

args.name: cache_dir
args.note: null = platform cache directory (spec 5.4); env OPENTIDECONSTANTS_CACHE_DIR

args.name: offline
args.note: env OPENTIDECONSTANTS_OFFLINE: 1, true, yes or on (case-insensitive, trimmed) turns offline on; when it does, the env wins and an explicit offline false does not turn it off

args.name: base_url
args.note: env OPENTIDECONSTANTS_BASE_URL; checked at construction (C: at the first otc_fetch_* call): not an absolute http or https URL is invalid_argument, never retried, no cache fallback

args.name: timeout
args.note: null = connect 10 s, read 60 s (spec 5.7); must be from 0.001 to 1e6 seconds, otherwise invalid_argument (0 and negatives included); C passes OTC_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT for the defaults, and 0 or any other value outside the range is OTC_E_INVALID_ARGUMENT

args.name: proxy

args.name: ca_file
args.note: null = SSL_CERT_FILE, else the system store; checked at construction: a ca_file or SSL_CERT_FILE that does not exist or cannot be read is io, never retried, no cache fallback; TypeScript in a browser: unsupported

args.name: user_agent
args.note: a suffix added to opentideconstants-{lang}/{version} (+https://opentideconstants.org); must be a string with no control characters (Python: also latin-1 only), otherwise invalid_argument at construction; ignored in a browser, which owns that header

args.name: logger

args.name: commercial_only

args.name: commercial_basis

members.note: Ruby OpenTideConstants.new(**options) and OpenTideConstants.open(**options) { |otc| }; Python OpenTideConstants(**options), usable as a context manager; TypeScript static async open(options) (a constructor cannot be async); C otc_open_file(path, &opts, &rel) opens a file only, and otc_fetch_latest / otc_fetch_release download first; a 200 pointer or index whose body is not JSON counts as a network error for on_network_error (spec 5.2 step 5); a failure to write the cached pointer is logged, not raised

members.name: last_error
members.note: the error behind loaded_from = cache_after_error; C: otc_last_error(rel, buf, len, &needed) gives the message of the last failure on the handle; any check that reaches the pointer (manual or automatic) clears it, and loaded_from does not change; a failed automatic update never escapes the query: it is logged with its stack and stored here, an SDK error as it is, any other failure as an SDK error with the original as cause (network for a transport failure, io otherwise)

members.name: latest
members.note: reads the latest pointer (OTC_latest-f{MAJOR}.json, or OTC_latest.json on a 404) with a conditional GET, and OTC_index.json too when the pointer's release is not readable by this SDK (spec 5.2 steps 2 and 2a); does not switch release; offline: offline_unavailable, no socket

members.name: check_for_update
members.note: offline: offline_unavailable, no socket; sets newer_format_major from OTC_latest.json (spec 7.4)

members.name: newer_format_major
members.note: set by check_for_update from OTC_latest.json (never the per-major pointer): its format major when it is newer than every supported major, else null (spec 7.4). When check_for_update fails with unsupported_format or reader_too_old because only newer-major releases exist, it is set before the error is raised; on a network error it keeps its earlier value (not reset before the GET)

members.name: update
members.note: Ruby update!; a Release held from before stays valid; offline: offline_unavailable, no socket, and no switch to a newer cached release. C: otc_fetch_update(&fopts, current, path, len, &needed, &updated): needed gets the path length with its NUL; path and len are checked before any network access, so a small buffer is buffer_too_small and downloads nothing; updated is true only when the newer release is in the cache and path names it

args.name: formats

members.note: spec 4.3.2: writes the data files in formats plus OTC_{D}.sha256 and OTC_{D}.meta.json into to; returns the paths written (an identical existing file is not written and not listed); TypeScript in a browser fails with unsupported; C without otc_fetch returns OTC_E_NOT_BUILT; with release latest and a network error, on_network_error use_cache (the default) writes the newest cached readable release, raise (or no usable cached release) raises network; cache when the cache lock cannot be taken (a stale lock not removed after 3 attempts); all or nothing: originals that a new file replaces are renamed aside and restored if any rename fails, and if a restore fails the error lists the paths that changed

members.name: verify
members.note: hashes the files again in full against OTC_{D}.sha256; C otc_verify_file(path, sha256_path, &err) is in the core library; a client with loaded_from file_unverified has no OTC_{D}.sha256: checksum_mismatch, message "no OTC_{D}.sha256 next to the file"

members.name: cached_releases

members.name: prune
members.note: never removes the loaded release; a cache operation: works on the configured cache, also on a client opened with file, and never touches the file's folder; a lock at least 120 s old is stale and is taken, so a crashed process's release is pruned; stops at the first release it cannot remove and fails with cache, reporting the releases removed before it (Ruby, Python, TypeScript: CacheError removed; C: the output array and count)

DNS, TLS, connection or timeout failure, an HTTP 5xx after the retries, or a body shorter than its Content-Length; also on_network_error raise with an empty cache, a 200 pointer or index whose body is not JSON (a captive portal), more than 5 redirects, a redirect from https to http, and a 404 for a data file that OTC_{D}.sha256 lists (status 404, "file listed in OTC_{D}.sha256 is missing on the server"); also a 200 pointer, index or .sha256 whose body is not valid for its type (the wrong JSON shape, or a checksum list with no valid row), which never replaces the stored copy
HTTP 404 for a pinned datestamp
offline mode and no usable cached release, or releases() offline and no cached index (a network failure with on_network_error raise is the network error)

a SHA-256 or size does not match, or the pointer and the .sha256 file disagree; also verify on a client with loaded_from file_unverified ("no OTC_{D}.sha256 next to the file"); also an eager download whose .sha256 has no .json row ("not listed"), and C otc_open_file with require_checksum and no .sha256
format_version major not supported
the release's release.min_reader_version is newer than SUPPORTED_FORMAT_VERSION; the message names both versions

not JSON, a required field missing, or a reference does not resolve; also a repeated station_id across active stations and tombstones, a repeated tombstone id, a repeated (system, alias id) pair, a repeated set_id, convention_id or licence_id, a format_version or min_reader_version present but not MAJOR.MINOR, a string with an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate, a datestamp counter longer than 9 digits from the server, and a stream index entry whose line has a different station_id (the message names index-v1.json); also a licence whose attribution is not a string or whose provider is neither a string nor null, a malformed created or record_span time, a pointer or index file entry without a string sha256 and a non-negative integer size, a .sha256 with a repeated name or invalid UTF-8, a repeated constituent name within a set, and a release.datestamp that does not match the datestamp grammar
require_station with an unknown id
require_station with a removed id
update on a client opened on a pinned release or a file

the cache cannot be written (permissions, disk full, a failed rename), or a stale lock cannot be removed after 3 attempts; a failure to write the cached pointer is logged, not this error; also a cached file that is there but cannot be read (CR2 DR16), for example the cached OTC_index.json that releases reads offline
download found a file in to with the same name and a different SHA-256, and overwrite is false
TypeScript in a browser: an operation that needs a file system (download), and the options proxy and ca_file
a local file cannot be opened or read; a ca_file or SSL_CERT_FILE that does not exist or cannot be read; any call on a client after close ("the release is closed")

a bad datestamp (a counter longer than 9 digits from the caller too), lat or lon out of range, a negative radius, an empty query, or a NULL handle; also a limit of 0 or less, a file name that is not OTC_<D><ext>, a malformed proxy or base_url, file together with release, offline or on_network_error, and an unknown, removed or foreign station in attribution; also a timeout outside 0.001 to 1e6 seconds, a user_agent that is not a string or has a control character, and a null, unknown or foreign station in reference_station or subordinates_of; prediction (spec 5.4): start > stop, step_s <= 0 or not an integer, a bin_number that is not an integer or (outside C) is 0 or less, in C a negative bin_number, in every SDK a bin_number above 2^53 - 1, a naive datetime, a datum of the wrong type, a subordinate R height ratio of 0 or less (4.8 step 3), a set_id that names no set of the station, with commercial_only a set_id whose licence is non-commercial (the message names commercial_only), a height_adjusted_type other than R or A (the message names the value), and an astro table that fails the table check of 4.2a (a negative row speed or a malformed table; the message names the table and the row)

prediction: the set's qc_status is not ok or flagged (prediction spec 4.2 step 2), or the station has no usable recommended set (with commercial_only: no effective recommended set) and no offsets; when commercial_only removed the recommended set, the message names commercial_only
heights on a current set, or currents on a water-level set
the convention's v0_model or nodal_handling is not implemented (prediction spec 4.2); its C status number 18 is fixed since phase 1 (CR D24)

the convention's astro_table_id names no table in the release, or the convention has no astro_table_id; message: release {datestamp} has no astro table "{id}" for convention "{convention_id}". Format 1.0 requires astro_tables when a convention uses f_u_at_prediction (since the schema revision of site PR #45); this file was written before that revision or is invalid. ({id} is "" when the convention has none)
a constituent of the set has no astro table row (or a name with no row in an Astro function)
an instant outside the table's years, including the padding of prediction spec 4.6, 4.8 and 4.9; never for an empty window (4.1)

the requested datum needs a value the set does not give (prediction spec 4.5); or, at a subordinate station, the reference has a usable set from the offsets' source but that set has no published chart datum or lacks the requested datum (4.8 step 2)
the bin is not in the set or in the offsets

a series (heights, heights_at, currents) at a station predicted by the event method: a subordinate tide station whose high and low offsets differ (prediction spec 4.8a), or any subordinate current station; at a tide station it comes after every other check of 4.8 step 6

to_local or otc_tz_open cannot get zone rules at run time: Python has no system database and no tzdata; Ruby has no tzinfo (or no tzinfo-data where the system has no database); C has local time compiled in but the zone directory otc_tz_open resolves (TZDIR, else /usr/share/zoneinfo) cannot be read; TypeScript's Intl has no time-zone support; the message names what to install (C: the directory it tried)
the zone name is not in the database in use, or the shared name rules of prediction spec 4.1 reject it; in C also a name that fails the IANA name pattern or has no TZif file in the resolved directory

the reference is missing or removed, or has no reference set (no usable set from the offsets' source, 4.8 step 1; no usable current set with the reference bin, 4.9 step 1), or, with commercial_only, the offsets' licence or the reference set's licence is non-commercial (the message names the licence)

error_base_class.note: every error class is a direct subclass of the base and of nothing else; every error has .code; a system error that causes an SDK error is kept as the cause; the userinfo of every URL in an error message or a log line is replaced with ***@

SUPPORTED_FORMAT_VERSION.note: the newest format version this SDK reads (spec 7.4); equals supported_format_version in the package's supported-formats.json

environment.OPENTIDECONSTANTS_OFFLINE: offline (1, true, yes or on, case-insensitive and trimmed; it wins over an explicit offline false)

c_structs.note: C structs of the prediction API that no manifest object maps (prediction spec 5.2): each must be a typedef with these members, and init names its initialiser. A struct pending for C must not be declared yet.

otc_predict_opts.note: step_s int64_t (600), datum const char * (NULL = default), set_id const char * (NULL = recommended), bin_number int64_t (0 = default), otc_prediction_info *info (NULL = not wanted); defined also without otc_predict, so callers compile

otc_local_t.note: int64_t t; int32_t utc_offset_s; char local_time[32]; filled by otc_tz_local

pending_port.note: Prediction (prediction spec 5) names an SDK does not have yet, per language. Each API check treats a pending name as absent and fails if it is present; a name that is not pending must be present. A port removes its language's names in the change that adds them. Every pending name must be a manifest name that applies to the language (an object, an Object.member, an enum, an error code, and for C a c_structs name). Exception (CR D24): for C a pending error's otc_status value may be present or absent, so that its number can be fixed early (OTC_E_UNSUPPORTED_CONVENTION = 18); a pending C function, type, struct or enum value must be absent.
